The front door electric windows are operated by switches on the facia, and are connected in accordance with the following diagram. 1 - Body Computer node 2 - Left front electric window motor 3 - Right front electric window motor 4 - Left front control switch 5 - Right front control switch They may be controlled both manually and automatically, in accordance with the following logic: manual operation is by pressing the control switch for between 50 ms and 300 ms; automatic operation is by pressing the control switch for over 300 ms. The operation of the electric window is interrupted in the following cases: when automatic movement is in progress and the control switch is pressed again (opening or closing); at the end of travel (top or bottom), in both automatic and manual movement. When the ignition is switched off, the electric windows function is active for about 2 minutes, in manual mode only. - When one of the two doors is opened, this function is inhibited.

There are three door opening/closing systems on the Fiat Gingo: MECHANICAL DOOR OPENING/CLOSING The key used is a coded desmodromic type which matches the car's lock pawls. The key allows the locking/unlocking of the doors and opening of the tailgate from outside the vehicle by means of the pawl present on each of the front doors and the tailgate. OPENING/CLOSING DRIVER'S DOOR AND PASSENGER'S DOOR There is a pawl on the driver's and passenger's door handles which, by means of the mechanical key, enables the individual door to be locked/unlocked. OPENING/CLOSING TAILGATE This happens by inserting and rotating the key in the specific pawl on the handle. This will allow the tailgate to be released and then opened. For closing, simply push the tailgate into the closed position. LOCKING/UNLOCKING DOORS FROM CAR INTERIOR On the internal trim of all the doors, there is a push-pull handle for manually controlling the locking of the individual door from inside the interior compartment. ELECTRIC OPENING/CLOSING WITH KEY The system allows the locks on all the doors to be controlled, except for the tailgate. OPENING/CLOSING DOORS FROM THE OUTSIDE The door locks can be locked/unlocked centrally by insertign the key in the pawl present only on the driver's door, and turning it. Locking is indicated by the position on the internal handle (push-pull type), positioning it on each door. If the locking of a door is requested and one or several doors are open, repulsion takes place and the doors remain unlocked. OPENING/CLOSING TAILGATE The opening/closing of the tailgate is mechanical and takes place by the insertion and rotation of the key in the specific pawl on the handle. This will allow the tailgate to be released and then opened. For closing, simply push the tailgate into the closed position. LOCKING/UNLOCKING LOCKS FROM INSIDE When the internal handle on the driver's door is pressed, all the doors are locked centrally. If a handle on another door is operated, that individual door is locked locally. If a front door handle is operated with the door open, the mechanical action is not carried out and the door cannot be locked: this prevents the keys being accidentally locked manually inside the car. When the internal handle on the driver's door is pulled, all the doors are unlocked centrally. ELECTRICAL OPENING/CLOSING WITH REMTE CONTROL The system enables the locks on all the doors and tailgate to be controlled. RADIOFREQUENCY REMOTE CONTROL AND RELEVANT FUNCTIONS The system for central opening/locking the doors and tailgate uses a radiofrequency remote control capable of operating at a distance of up to 20 metres from the car (with free field). The remote control comprises: mechanical insert (key); 3 control buttons; an indicator LED. The control buttons are dedicated to: unlocking doors and tailgate, with a single short press; at the same time the courtesy light comes on for a fixed time and the direction indicators flash twice to confirm the event; locking doors and tailgate, with a single short press; at the same time the courtesy light goes out and the direction indicators flash once to confirm the event; opening tailgate, with a long press (over 1 second) because the action must be voluntary and not accidental, the tailgate is released; at the same time the direction indicators flash twice to confirm the event. After being opened, when re-closed, the tailgate returns to its previous state: If the car was unlocked, the tailgate returns to the unlocked state; if the car was locked, the tailgate returns to the locked state, in line with the door status. OPENING TAILGATE BY SOFT TOUCH ELECTRICAL HANDLE Coupled with the remote control, there is a soft-touch electrical handle on the tailgate handle, near the number plate light. This handle can be operated when the tailgate is in the released state (the tailgate is automatically released when the doors are unlocked centrally). In this situation, the electric handle is enabled and it is then possible to open the tailgate by operating it; the lock disengages, releasing the tailgate so it can be lifted. When the tailgate is instead in the locked state (the tailgate is automatically locked when the doors are locked), the tailgate cannot be opened by the electric handle and so the tailgate will remain closed. 1 - Instrument panel 2 - Tailgate opening control 3 - Boot opening electromagnet 4 - Ignition key 5 - Boot opening button LOCKING/UNLOCKING DOORS AND TAILGATE WITH KEY FROM OUTSIDE In addition to using the remote control, the locking/unlocking mechanisms can also be activated by the key operating the pawl in the driver's door or the tailgate pawl (for opening the tailgate only). LOCKING/UNLOCKING LOCKS FROM INSIDE When the internal handle on the driver's door is pressed, all the doors are locked centrally. If a handle on another door is operated, that individual door is locked locally. If a front door handle is operated with the door open, the mechanical action is not carried out and the door cannot be locked: this prevents the keys being accidentally locked manually inside the car. When the driver's door internal handle is pulled, all the doors and the tailgate are unlocked centrally. If the locking of a door is requested and one or several doors are open, repulsion takes place and the doors remain unlocked. This action is indicated by appropriate flashing of the direction indicators. CENTRAL LOCKING SYSTEM ADDITIONAL FUNCTIONS On versions which have both a Super instrument panel and a remote control, the automatic locking of the doors and tailgate can be set during driving. The function, activated via the instrument panel, automatically locks the doors and tailgate when the car exceeds the speed of 20 km/h. When the speed falls to below 20 km/h, the doors and tailgate remain locked, preventing unauthorised persons from gaining access from outside. The tailgate is always locked when the speed of 20 km/h is exceeded. The function is not activated in default. UNLOCKING LOCKS IN THE CASE OF AN ACCIDENT (ON VERSIONS WITH ELECTRIC LOCKING) In the case of a crash, the locks are automatically unlocked via the inertia switch to allow rescue workers to gain access to the interior compartment from outside. CHECK PANEL (ON VERSIONS WITH ELECTRIC LOCKING) The check panel function is carried out by the display on the instrument panel which warns the driver if one or more doors or the tailgate are not shut properly. IN AN EMERGENCY If the car battery does not deliver sufficient energy to the door locking electrical system (either because the battery is discharged or following an accident), the doors can be operated mechanically to open them. There are the following mechanical backups: mechanical connection on external handles with door unlocked, by operating the handle (for emergency access from the outside) mechanical connection in internal handles with integrated safe unlock (so the interior compartment can be abandoned in an emergency) mechanical unlocking of front doors by pawl using key (to gain access through the door if the car is locked) mechanical unlocking of tailgate by pawl using key. CHILD SAFETY There is a mechanism on both rear doors for mechanical engaging/disengaging the child safety lock. When the child safety lock is on, the rear doors cannot be opened in the interior compartment by operating the internal handles. These doors can only be opened from the outside with the door unlocked. However, the lock can always be locked/unlocked using the push-pull handle. The child safety lock on/off status is not indicated.

The car features two compartment lids, i.e. the bonnet lid and the fuel filler flap. The bonnet lid consists of an exterior trim assembled on a support frame. Strips of sealant are applied between the trim and the frame. These limit vibrations while also increasing overall rigidity. The fuel filler flap is made out of plastic in the same shade as the body and is moved by hand. A press-fastener is fitted to hold the flap in closed position. BONNET LID The bonnet lid is made using conventional pressing methods. Its frame includes preset collapse lines. This safety feature - together with special retaining hooks - prevents the bonnet going through the windscreen in the case of impact. The bonnet is lined throughout with a preformed panel in sound-absorbent material. This reduces noise emissions to the outside of the car and also to the car interior to increase passenger comfort. To lower aerodynamic noise still further, the front and rear sides of the engine bay are fitted with two seals. Moulded foam blocks are also fitted behind the two hinges. The panel is fastened to the frame by means of press-studs and is made out of compressed textile fibres coated with oil and water-repellent material that is preformed by hot-pressing. The pressing process includes the perimeter finish and holes for fastening. The lid is supported by two hinges, each fitted with a fastening hook made out of the moving part of the hinge. The lid is opened and closed by a single central catch that incorporates a safety hook. The catch is opened by a Bowden cable operated by a lever located in the lower side area of the facia on the driver's side. The flap hinge mount is secured by two nuts accessible from inside the wheel arch, and supports a flap return spring. On the inside of the flap, there are two pins which fit into a seating to maintain the correct closing position.

All vehicles can be fitted as an option with a large Skydome sun-roof with two glass panels, one fixed and the other mobile. The sun-roof is adjustable by means of a selector to nine positions in addition to the closed position. This allows the air flow around the passenger compartment to be optimised. To ensure safety during movement, the sun-roof is fitted with an anticrush safety device that cuts out movement in the presence of obstacles. The sunroof unit is all-in one. The glazed area extends in direction Y from the right channel to the left. It extends far enough in direction X to replace 70% of the roof area. The glazed surface is split into two panels, a tinted fixed panel at the rear and a tinted sliding panel at the front. The front panel is operated by a one-touch switch adjustable by means of a selector to 9 positions (three tiling or spoiler - Z, six sliding -X) plus closed position by means of an electric motor. A sealing strip around the opening of the sun-roof sliding section is in contact with the roof profile. This abuts against the front sliding panel profile. The roof is fitted with two manually-operated sliding sun blinds (roller blinds) that screen out the light. The selector is located on the front courtesy light and controls the electric operating motor by means of a control unit. The sun-roof is moved by the motor pinion that pulls two flexible racks to which are anchored the guides that pull the expanding pulleys that support the sun-roof sliding panel. To limit possible damage to passengers or objects caused by the roof when in movement, an anticrush function is active during roof closure, when the panel is sliding and also during tilt manoeuvres. The figure shows the sun-roof components 1 - Frame 2 - Frame reinforcement 3 - Front roller stop 4 - Rear roller stop 5 - Rear roller catch 5 - Rear roller catch 7 - Front glass 8 - Sliding glass front reinforcement 9 - Sliding glass rear reinforcement 10 - Rear glass 11 - Rack guides _ 23 - Weather strips 12 - Roller set sun blind 13 - Front roller lock plate 14 - Sunblind panel slide guides 15 - Deflector 16 - Motor with CTA 17 - Deflector guard 18 - Frame seal 19 - Front roller mounts 20 - Rear roller mounts 21 - Rear sunblind end travel block 22 - Slide mechanism guides 23 - Weather strips 24 - Slide mechanisms The system consists of: an electric displacement motor with Hall-effect position and speed sensors; a frame with two compartments, the rear for the fixed panel, the front for the sliding panel. The slide mechanism is a flexible rack system; an electronic control unit built into the electric motor assembly; a selector (one touch) used to move the sun-roof to different positions. The opening front panel is opened by operating the one-touch open/close switch/selector on the front central courtesy light. This supplies the motor to turn the pinion that draws the rack along the guide on the frame. The motor moves flexible pulling racks housed in seats on the frame. These are anchored to extending mechanisms that support the sun-roof, which is moved to the required point or position. The sun-roof is equipped with an underlying blind that can be slid along by hand by means of a handle. This is designed to keep out sunlight. Sun blind The front and rear polyester blind to keep out sunlight are sliding, roller type. They can only be operated manually and slide in guides supported by Teflon slide pads interspersed with rubber bearings between pad and guide. These are equipped with a handle at the front that can be grasped with a catch to hold the blind open. The sun-roof may be moved manually by means of the selector under the following conditions: Roof opening. Roof opening with key-on. With key-on, the front glass panel is opened in AUTOMATIC mode if the button is pressed for longer than 300 msec. The mechanism moves the glass from fully closed to fully open in spoiler position. When you press the same side of the button again for >300 ms, the front glass pane moves to fully open position. After the initial opening command, the front glass panel may be stopped in intermediate positions by pressing the button again. The front glass panel may be opened in MANUAL mode by pressing on the side of the button for <60 to <300 ms. The front glass panel moves from fully closed in proportion to the time the button is pressed from <60 and <300 ms. It stops in this position when the button is released. When the same side of the button is pressed again, within a time period between <60 and <300 ms, the front glass panel moves step by step to fully open position. This function allows the front panel to be moved to intermediate positions between the positions achievable automatically. Roof closure Roof closure with key-on; The front glass roof panel closes AUTOMATICALLY when one side of the button is pressed for >300 ms. The front glass roof panel moves from fully open to swivel open position. When the button is pressed on the same side for > 300 ms, the front glass panel moves to closed position. The front glass roof panel closes MANUALLY when one side of the button is pressed for <60 to <300 ms. The front glass panel moves from fully open in proportion to the time the button is pressed from <60 and <300 ms and stops in the position where the button is released. When the same side of the button is pressed again, within a time period between <60 and <300 ms, the front glass panel moves step by step to closed position. This function can be used to position the front panel in intermediate positions between the automatic closure positions. Automatic closure can be interrupted at any time by pressing the selector upward (inhibition position) or altering selector position (it is locked in this case). A new command can be given after 10 do not disconnect the battery or sun-roof power supply. If this happens, the control unit loses its memory and must be reset as described in the relevant paragraph. ANTIPINCH FUNCTION To limit possible damage to passengers or objects caused by the roof when in movement, an anticrush function is active during roof closure, when the panel is sliding (X) and also during tilt (Z) manoeuvres. If effort in excess of a given threshold is detected, the control unit interprets this as an obstacle and stops movement immediately before moving the roof back by about 10 cm if it is sliding - or in the fully open position if it is tilting. The anticrush protection can be cut out by setting the selector to the inhibition position as follows: select the required position; press the selector down vertically and hold down during movement until the selected position is achieved. SELECTOR View of ONE-TOUCH control selector (1 - Closed position (2 - Tilted open position CTA CONTROL UNIT Sun-roof movement is controlled by an electronic control unit housed in the casing integral with the motor. The unit processes signals from the selector or remote control via the body computer and also controls the anticrush protection function. The function is controlled by the control unit, which receives position and speed information from Hall effect sensors fitted to the crankshaft. When effort in excess of a certain threshold is detected, corresponding to a higher current uptake and a reduction in engine rpm after a time, this is interpreted as an obstacle. The CTA then stops the roof immediately and moves it back in the opposite direction by about 100 mm. The control unit also receives a vehicle speed signal because the vacuum created at certain speeds could change the effort required to close the roof and under certain conditions this could be interpreted as an impediment. The control unit therefore uses this signal to ensure movement is not halted inadvertently. +30 direct from battery: +15 Key-on: Signals (down) from switch Signals (up) from switch Dedicated odometer signal Earth RESETTING THE CONTROL UNIT MEMORY The electronic control unit for the sun roof can lose the memory containing the positions as a result of a break in supply during roof movements. Proceed as follows to reset the memory: Turn the ignition key in the ON position Move the selector to closed position When you keep the button pressed in this position, the roof closes in steps Keep holding the button down and wait for the roof to close fully and the motor to stop Release the button: initialisation complete The procedure for restoring the memory should be carried out, if there are no impediments, in case there are problems with the sliding of the roof detected by the control unit. During the memory reset procedure, the control unit again stores the mechanical effort required for sliding. EMERGENCY MANOEUVRE The sunroof motor is housed in the middle of the roof. The fixed body windows, windscreen and rear side windows are bonded flush with the body. Together with the rear window, they help increase the structural rigidity of the body and increase the level of car safety while greatly reducing aerodynamic noise. WINDSCREEN The windscreen glass is tinted and laminated. It consists of two layers of glass with a sheet of plastic in between. This configuration prevents the glass layers from shattering if struck by stones and pebbles. This maintains visibility and above all ensures a high degree of protection if the window is struck by an occupant's head. The window border that overlaps the body is screen-printed in black. The windscreen is fitted, on some versions, with a rain sensor bonded near the rear view mirror mount base and a demisting sensor located on the base itself a few millimetres away from the windscreen. REARSCREEN The rear window is made out of tempered, not laminated, glass and bonded flush with the tail-gate structure. A set of demisting rheophores on the inner surface of the rear window include a hole at the bottom for the rear wiper axle seat, a reference and the wiper parking area. The rheophore is connected to the electrical system by means of two terminals located on the right and left sides of the rheophore. The rear window border that overlaps the tail-gate structure is screen-printed in black. FIXED SIDE WINDOWS The fixed side windows are made out of tinted tempered glass and bonded flush with the body. A sealing strip on the pillar side of the windows prevents turbulence and wind noise with the door closed. The area where the side window fits to the tailgate structure is screen-printed in black.

All vehicle interior trim is designed to satisfy severe international flame-resistance standards. The main components are slow-burning: they do not ignite due to accidental contact (for example, if a cigarette is dropped), flames do not develop and, in the presence of fierce heat they burn to produce strong, dense smoke. Trim design and configuration is aimed at producing a high level of acoustic comfort combined with a high degree of passive safety. All the protrusions that could harm car occupants in the case of impact have been eliminated. Symbols describing the correct use of the baby seat in the presence of a passenger air bag are shown on the inner side of the passenger side sun visor . Characteristic of working principle 5580C air bag system FRONT COURTESY LIGHT View of front courtesy light 1 - Front courtesy light FRONT COURTESY LIGHT The front courtesy light comprises a rocker switch, and it contains a light bulb. The courtesy light is switched on/off as follows: to switch on the courtesy light permanently, press the switch on the right; to switch off the courtesy light, press the switch on the left; for automatic management from the body computer node, keep the switch in the central position. The body computer node switches the courtesy light on in the following conditions: when any door (front or rear) is opened, for a maximum of 3 minutes; it is reactivated whenever a door is opened; when the ignition key is removed, for a maximum of 10 seconds; when the doors are unlocked (by the remote control or the driver's/passenger's door catch), for a maximum of 15 minutes; when the ignition is turned off, for a maximum of 10 seconds; when the inertial switch intervenes, for a maximum of 15 minutes. The body computer node automaticallly switches off the courtesy light under the following conditions: when the ignition is turned on; when the doors are unlocked (by the remote control or the driver's/passenger's door catch); when the inertia switch is reset. The rear courtesy light is switched on or off respectively when the tailgate is opened or closed.

The front seats have been designed to optimize comfort and safety and ensure maximum driving comfort, ideal lateral containment properties and lumbar support. The base structure is fastened to the seat lift unit and is made out of pressed steel with an antisubmarining ridge. This prevents the occupant from sliding under the lap part of the seat belt if the car decelerates abruptly. The squab frame is made out of a pressed steel structure that improves energy absorption in the case of rear impact. This is anchored to the seat lift unit by means of a bilateral joint. On two-door versions, the squab can be tilted by means of the release handle, which allows the seat to tilt and glide forward in a single manoeuvre. Subsquent repositioning is aided by a memory mechanism in the slide guides. This allows the seat to be restored to its initial position automatically. Squab rake may be adjusted by turning a knob on the inside near the joint, while the lumbar adjustment control is halfway along the squab, also on the inside. The squab supports a height-adjustable head restraint. This can be moved through a travel of about 50 mm by means of a release button located on the right side of the head restraint. The seat lift unit consists of a steel frame that includes the lift mechanism. The slide guides are secured to the lift mechanism, cushion and squab. The seat belt branch (fitted with the fastening sensor on the driver's seat) is secured to the inner side of the seat lift unit. Driver's seat reach may be adjusted through a travel of 230 mm along angled guides. Seat ride may be adjusted through a travel of 60 mm by means of a new type of mechanism that moves the seat in an arc (a maximum height movement corresponds to a horizontal forward movement of about 50 mm). This mechanism is operated by a ratchet lever. The passenger's seat comprises a removable trinket compartment, in the bottom. The rear seats are fitted with squabs built to ensure maximum occupant safety in the case of various types of impact. They also prevent items in the luggage compartment from being propelled forward. The squab and seat may be of different types, one-piece seat and squab with central head restraint and slide function, with split seat and squab with slide function and squab with adjustable tilt. The squab recline catches are located near the joint. The rear cushions come with a pressed steel base with antislip profile that forms an effective antisubmarining structure in conjunction with the beam welded to the rear floor pan. On the sliding version, the slide mechanisms are located to the body floorpan. On certain versions, the rear seat squab may be split and reclined separately 40/60%. Certain versions come with a third head restraint for the central seat with the same specifications. Versions with a third head restraint also come with a central inertia reel seat belt. On certain versions, the rear seats may be sliding with adjustable squab recline. The front and rear bumpers are made out of polypropylene and contain impact absorbing buffers. The wheel arch housings are protected by semirigid plastic shields that protect the inner part of the compartment from external objects and offer partial acoustic insulation, while acting as a trim element for visible parts in the wheel arch housing. The lower part of the engine compartment is protected by a cover fixed to the chassis and the bumper and, in the upper section there is a series of covers which can be easily detached for maintenance and repair operations. The other elements (grilles, badges, trims, etc.) are designed to enhance the appearance and spirit of the vehicle. COMPOSITION Absorbent buffers are fitted on all car versions: two on the front strut connection beam and three on the rear trim near middle of the bumper and the two rails. The buffers are made out of expanded polypropylene. This material is resistent to temperature changes, ageing and deformation.

The car is fitted with seat belts with three anchorage points. As an option, the third rear passenger seat can also be fitted with a belt with automatic inertia reel. The height-adjustable front seat belts are fitted with electrically-operated pretensioners with load limiter. There is a sensor, on the branch anchoring the belt to the driver's seat which warns when the seat belt is not fastened by means of a warning light in the instrument panel (with the ignition ON). On all the rear seat places, in versions so fitted out, there are seat belts with three anchorage points and inertia reel, mounted on the roof pillars, or the roof itself for the central place. General remarks The topics are covered with particular attention to the new technical features required for passing the various tests introduced by new legislation. The descriptions and operating information provided are limited to a discussion of principles, rules and minimum precautions. For information on repair methods and vehicle specifications, see the specific sections on repair procedures. Aerodynamics The styling of the new car is designed to reflect great personality and originality and improves on the attributes of roominess, practicality and sturdiness achieved by previous models. The front, sides, rear and underbody were developed with particular attention to aerodynamics and allow outstanding drag coefficient values. The following values are an example: Version with basic specification drag coefficient Cd - 0.33 drag coefficient by area Cd x A = 0.6738 These values are the result of road testing and measurements carried out in a wind tunnel. These results contribute to the noiselessness of the vehicle and significantly reduce wind noise. They also allow fuel saving. Safety The main aim of car manufacturers is definitely the total safety of the driver and passengers. To adapt the vehicle to highly demanding European and international market regulations, the new vehicle was designed with great attention to detail in order to achieve an optimum response in all situations. Specifications The vehicle's great torsional and flexural rigidity ensure good properties of passive strength and also offer a number of benefits: low noise due to fewer vibrations; no creaking from the trim; better handling by maintaining the correct suspension angles and thus an absolutely controlled drive for a sensation of stability and comfort in general, greater ability to withstand breakages caused by using the vehicle over particularly uneven road surfaces; sensation of vehicle compactiness; to ensure long-term overall vehicle quality. Torsional rigidity Diagram showing deformation due to torsion Torsional rigidity Torsional rigidity values Body with bonded windscreen: 60100 daNm/rad Flexural rigidity Diagram showing deformation due to bending Flexural rigidity Flexural rigidity values Body with bonded windscreen: 860 daN/mm Preventive safety This concerns all factors that determine comfortable driving conditions and prevent situations that could distract the driver's attention: very stiff body for greater driving safety; optimised engine mountings (barycentric) to minimise vibration and noise transmission; climate control system (where fitted) with activated charcoal pollen filter with balanced diffusion throughout the passenger compartment. Well-arranged ventilation outlets allow excellent air exchange and improved transpiration and thermal comfort; an extensive glazed area allows optimum visibility; the tail-lights are shaped to optimise the indicator light functions; the arrangement of the pedals, steering wheel (height-adjustable as an option), main controls and warning lights has been carefully considered to achieve a good valance between driving position and ability to reach the controls; the height-adjustable driver's seat (where fitted) allows the best possible driving position to be achieved; generous interior dimensions allow the vehicle occupants the necessary level of comfort; abundant use of sound-absorbent materials and the adoption of specific vibration-proof fasteners to reduce mechanical noise and achieve a noiseless, welcoming environment; interior trim that meets the toughest flame-retardant standards. Active safety This concerns features of the vehicle and specific components that help the driver overcome potential dangers while driving. The following features contribute to the vehicle's active safety: outstanding stability during driving and in terms of the vehicle's dynamic performance; excellent braking system; good pick-up; The vehicle offers features that are mutually complementary: the front suspension ensures great control of the vehicle during standard or sporty driving. It allows great driving precision and vehicle control over wet and slippery surfaces, a prompt, accurate response and an ability to absorb obstacles and roughness present on the road surface; a torsion beam rear suspension designed to offer improved handling performance, the torsion beam assures the susension an ideal level of torsional rigidity for an excellent balance between vehicle front and rear. smart bushes attaching the rear axle to the body for limited self-adjustment to steering modulated by the stiffness of the bushes new design electric steering system (where fitted) designed for a crisp, prompt response in all situations; braking system big enough to guarantee powerful, safe braking without fade, consisting of two independent cross-over circuits with an ABS/EBD system (the most advanced brake control system currently available) with four channels and four active sensors to reduce activation times, equipped with an EBD (Electronic Brake Distribution) device: that does away with the need for a load proportioning valve; VDC integrated traction control system with ESP/ASR/HHC functions (where fitted). Passive safety Because in statistical terms head-on impacts account for 60% of accidents, side impacts account for 30% and the remaining 10% are accounted for by shunts, fires and rolls, the vehicle structure has been designed and developed to crumple in controlled manner in the case of impact and to absorb the energy developed without affecting the living areas of the passenger compartment. To safeguard the vehicle occupants, the seat anchorage points and seat belt attachment points (a three-part belt is also available on the central rear seat) have been reinforced. Front seat occupants are protected, as standard, by a system that includes a driver's airbag and pyrotechnic seat belt pretensioners (electronically controlled). As an option, the safety system may be complemented by a passenger airbag (that can be deactivated manually by inserting the ignition key in a barrel on the right facia head), sidebags for the driver and front passenger and a head bag that extends under the moulded roof along the right and left sides to protect the heads of vehicle occupants from side impact. Particular attention was devoted to structural design to minimise damage and repair costs arising as a result of accidents If the body is repaired, the structural reinforcements should always be replaced if deformed. General specifications The body is made up of differential crumple zones and is fitted with reinforcements to strengthen the survival cell. These enable the car to withstand head-on impact by ensuring the passenger compartment remains intact to offer the greatest protection to its occupants and minimise the effects of impact. The main actions taken on the body to achieve the required aims are as follows: front structure with differential crumple zones designed to crumple at pre-established points to absorb and distribute the impact force over the structure due to a front sacrificial beam bolted to a crash box that can absorb even off-centre impact. reinforcements on the side pillars connected to a high-strength tubular steel structure under the facia that ensures a sturdy connection between the pillars and also with the floor, to which it is connected by a cradle anchored to the tunnel. This configuration contributes significantly to ensuring the non-deformability of the entire front area of the passenger compartment during head-on and side impacts. Because it also acts as a support structure for the steering column, it prevents the steering wheel moving back and upwards during all types of frontal impact. reinforcements under the floorpan that increase the solidity and stiffness of the floor to limit deformation as much as possible; adoption of bonnet retaining hooks on the bonnet hinges and a collapsible telescopic steering column. Impact forces are further absorbed and distributed by the engine attachments that discharge the forces to the front reinforcement and prevent excessive load on the passenger compartment. These features of the structure, together with the fastening systems and the interior energy absorbing parts allow the vehicle to achieve a high level of safety and pass all the tests imposed by standards. The above has been achieved by: reinforcing the underdoor reails between the front pillars and the central pillars; reinforcing the central and rear pillars at the rail attachment points, at the seat belt anchorage points and in the lock striker areas; inserting a box section reinforcement beam between the underdoor rails. the doors described below contribute significantly to the vehicle's ability to withstand side impact. Composition . 1 Underdoor rail reinforcement 2 Reinforcement beam between underdoor rails General specifications The door structure is of fundamental importance to the safety of passengers in the case of side impact and the door panel geometry and stiffness is therefore designed to maintain survival spaces at the sides and minimise possible injury to passengers. The above has been achieved by: fitting tubular side impact bars, using reinforcements at the waistline and along the pillars to make up an ideal high-strength door ring; fitting high-strength locks and strikers; fitting energy-absorbing interior door trim without sharp corners designed to ensure minimum impact against the body in the event of an accident. Composition . 1 Pillar reinforcement 2 Tubular side-impact bar General specifications The specific structure of the ceiling makes the passenger compartment more rigid and contributes to passenger safety in the event of side impact or roll-over which, despite being much less likely to occur than the other types of impact, is one of the most dangerous accidents. The following features increase the solidity of the passenger compartment structure: high-resistance steel box section crossmembers connecting the side panels at the upper part of the windscreen, tailgate and in a central position between the upper ends of the pillars; structural adhesive sections along the edges of the upper box section beams of the windscreen compartment and tail-gate compartment. These features allow outstanding levels of strength to be achieved during the static and dynamic crushing and rollover tests required by European standards. Composition . 1 Upper windscreen box section beam 2 Upper tailgate box section beam 3 Roof panel 4 Box section beam connecting central pillars General specifications The vehicle's resistance to rear impact is very high and passes the tests specified by the toughest standards in force in Europe. This performance is ensured by: a reinforced rear box section beam; reinforcements on the attachments between the rear beam and pillars; tailgate with reinforced ribbing; reinforced side and rear tailgate ribbing. Composition . 1 Left rear rail 2 Right rear rail 3 Rail connection beam 4 Rear beam WINDSCREEN AND WINDOWS The fixed windows further contribute to safety. The windscreen is bonded to the body and this increases the structural rigidity of the vehicle. To increase the vehicle safety level, the windscreen is in laminated glass. This solution prevents the glass from shattering if struck by stones or gravel to assure visibility at all times and above all to offer a high level of protection if struck with the head. The windscreen is bonded to the body. The seal flush with the body helps reduce wind noise due to the vehicle's progress. Safety against fires This is achieved by a FPS (Fire Prevention System) consisting of: fireproof interiors, all trim meets the toughest US flame-retardant standards and will not catch fire if it accidentally touches a heat source (e.g. a cigarette) and limits the flame propagation rate; inertia switch to cut off the fuel pump; antimisfiring shields (overheating of the catalytic converter, for petrol versions) that insulate the catalytic converter and protect the brake and fuel pipes; electrical equipment protected by maxifuses that cut off the fuel flow in the case of short-circuit or overheating that could occur in the event of fire; battery secured in the event of impact or roll-over; cut-off valve to prevent fuel leaks if the vehicle rolls over; plastic fuel tank with high mechanical strength and fire-resistance, secured firmly to the body in a shielded position; arrangement of the electrical equipment, fuel pipes and brakes designed to minimise the possible risk of fire in the event of accidents or failure. GENERAL SPECIFICATIONS To meet EEC standards, the vehicle's exterior noise levels must be lower than 74 decibels. Driving comfort and living conditions inside the passenger compartment have been improved by: optimising the body through a thorough examination of all parts subject to noise, which have been made stiffer and fastened more securely; choosing contact materials with great care; by improving the insulation against noise transmitted from the road surface, from mechanical parts and from the suspension; by taking great care over parts assembly, aerodynamics and all parts with shapes that affect acoustic comfort, such as door handles, door mirrors, bumpers and other outlines; by fitting new generation engines with high-tech features designed to improve acoustic/vibrational factors; by fitting a barycentric engine mounting. Another area of improvement has been the passenger compartment insulation. The following action has been taken: highly efficient sound-absorbent materials with optmum thickness and layout on the vehicle; fitting of a sound-absorbent undershield in the lower part of the engine compartment for acoustic insulation elimination of acoustic holes (areas where sound can pass between the engine compartment and passenger compartment) by fitting double-lipped seals, thicker rubber plugs, by fitting the various sound-insulation parts together more tightly to avoid uncovered areas; extensive use of sound-absorbent seals; sound-proofed coating of panels with heat-bonded materials applied before painting; lining of the bulkhead and front steps to remove the sensation of the engine's presence; application of heat-expanding materials inside the box sections prior to painting to reduce noise transmission. During body cataphoresis process, the volume of these materials expands ten times to fill the box section effectively. lining the boot compartment appropriately to reduce rolling noise; carefully examining the fitting and size of parts liable to squeak such as the facia, heater and seats: the anchorage and fastening points have been reinforced. To maintain the high level of acoustic comfort achieved, the specifications adopted during manufacture must be restored exactly in the event of repair. General remarks The vehicle body is designed to withstand for many years (8 years without perforating corrosion, 10 years without structural weakening) any environmental attack to the interior, not visible but potential subject to corrosion, and exterior, particularly subject to damage that may affect the exerior appearance of the vehicle. This result has been achieved by examining the structure of the interior panels to minimise their exposure to corrosive infiltrations, making extensive use of galvanised panels and using a host of protective treatments and seals on all interior and exterior panel surfaces to prevent leaks and fulfil an essential sound-proofing function. Galvanising The panels may be zinc coated by means of two different technological processes: galvanic deposition: the panel is painted with, if only one surface is treated (SINGLE GALVANISED PANEL) or immersed in, if both surfaces are treated (DOUBLE GALVANISED PANEL) a solution of zinc salts from which a layer of pure zinc with a high level of surface finish is deposited; hot deposition: molten zinc is deposited on the panel due to the effect of heat. During this process, which is used mainly for structural body parts, zinc thickness up to 20 microns can be achieved. This process is used for parts most exposed to corrosion while eight microns are normally used for other zinc-coated panels. The zinc layer acts as an active chemical protection for the steel, known as a sacrificial layer, that combines with the subsequent protective systems to guarantee outstanding long-term corrosion-proofing. 85% of the body by weight is made up of zinc-coated panels, of which 73% by weight double galvanised and 27% by weight in single galavanised steel. All parts making up the chassi are 100% galvanised with some parts, e.g. the suspension attachments and seat belt reinforcements, made out of panels with a high thickness of zinc. The outer and mobile parts of the body (linings and reinforcements) are made totally out of double galvanised steel with the exception of the ceiling, which is made out of ungalvanised steel because it is hardly exposed to corrosion. The use of galvanised steel for exterior panels minimises the risk of cosmetic corrosion during the first three years of the vehicle's life. Specifications A, paint product supplier; B, enamel colour and type C, code; D. type of product to be used for touching up and painting in the event of service operations Composition The aim of painting the bodyshell is to: protect the sheet metal against corrosion due to exposure to environmental effects; achieve high levels of gloss and colour richness and maintain them in time. Before painting, the body undergoes a bonderisation process when the body is cleaned of grease and surface rust by rinsing in a series of basic and then acid baths to prepare it for the subsequent painting stage. Painting is a fundamental treatment for the protection of structural parts. The process allows the paint to coat areas of the body that would otherwise be in accessible. The process is carried out by immersion in electrically insulated tanks containing an aqueous solution of paint product. This solution is negatively charged while the body is positively charged. During immersion, a layer of paint is deposited (25 microns on horizontal parts and 20 microns on vertical parts) that can be adjusted by altering the bath voltage, the bath temperature and the length of time the body remains in the solution. The body then undergoes a process of stoving in an oven at 160° for 18 minutes. Heat bonded materials are then applied to the prepared body and then all the joints between the body panels are sealed to prevent corrosive agents leaking through. An abrasion-resistant coating is then applied to all areas exposed to gravel from the road. This highly flexible protective coating bonds tightly to the surface and also contributes significantly to acoustic damping. The body is now prepared by adding a primer coat (50 microns thick) before undergoing a further stoving cycle in the oven. After the final painting cycle (followed by stoving in the oven), the corrosion-proofing treatments are complemented by the application of wax oil inside the box section parts. Re-apply the wax oil treatment if box section parts are replaced during service. MAIN SPECIFICATIONS According to EEC ELV (End of Life Vehicles) directives, all metallic and non-metallic parts must be recovered from the vehicle and reused, 80% to produce new material and 5% for recovered energy. Nowadays, some 75% of a vehicle's weight is made up of metal that can easily be recovered by melting when different metals can be separated by heating to their different melting points. All the remaining part of the vehicle, amounting to 25% by weight, must be recovered before this stage. The solution to the problem of recycling plastics is resolved at the design stage: the possibility of re-using the material on future components must be assessed at this time: The aims to be considered at the design stage include: ease of component disassembly; choice of noble materials in the recyclable polymer chain (giving priority to parts made up of a single family, e.g. PP). Recycling does not allow the production of a part that is the same as the original part because the material may not be able to guarantee the necessary levels of reliability or it may not be financially viable. Plastics may be recycled in a cascade pattern. For example: insulating material for the building industry is obtained from seat padding; the material used to line the wheel arches is obtained from the bumpers and then goes on to produce sound-proofing elements. In the end, it becomes a fuel for energy production. This model has been designed to ensure that all its plastic and elastomer parts (rubbers) weighing over 50 grams are marked with coded symbols to identify the material during recycling and also to ensure that all its components are recyclable. The recyling process therefore afffects three successive vehicle generations to help save raw materials. Other materal reuse processes are also being examined outside the motor industry, following the lead taken by the F.A.Re (Fiat Auto Recycling) partnership in the Eighties and Nineties. Another important point to note concerns the use of heavy metals in the motor industry. The metals in question are hexavalent chrome (Cr6), Mercury (Hg), Cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb). These are banned (Cr6) or permitted only in tiny amounts when their use must be indicated by labelling or by including information in the documents supplied with the vehicle. The tables in the chapter "GENERAL INFORMATION AND TECHNICAL DATA - OPERATING DATA" show symbols for and descriptions of recyclable materials present on the vehicle. This is to ensure that the best available products are used to wash the interior, paint plastic parts and carry out repairs, bonding etc. The aim is to avoid the possibility of damage by using incompatible products. Labelling also allows organic materials to be selected on the basis of their chemical composition. During service, it is also advisable to separate materials on the basis of their composition to ensure that they can be recycled more easily. Diagram showing the reuse of recycled materials . When the desired passenger side temperature is set, there is no corresponding flow of air at the required temperature. Results of the tests 1 CHECK ON CORRECT OPERATION OF CLIMATE CONTROL NODE All OK Problems encountered Operation With the engine on and the compressor off, place the control unit in the AUTO function (MONO button off) and adjust the temperature using the passenger side temperature knob moving it from cold to hot. Using the diagnostic equipment check that the engine temperature reaches at least 70 °C. Now carry out the operations for checking the passenger compartment cooling function: with the engine on, at ambient temperature of around 20 °C, with the vehicle compressor on, place the control unit to AUTO, adjust the temperature knob from hot to maximum cold LO, the distribution to the front position, the fan speed to 3 bars and the outside air intake function. Feel whether the air coming out of the vents changes (getting colder) in temperature. Then check for any errors relating to the solar sensor. The solar sensor reference values are less than 50 W/mq. a maximum difference between the driver and passenger selections of 7°C is permitted. Connect the diagnostic equipment (Examiner Plus or Smart) and carry out active diagnosis 'Zeroing phonic wheel initialisation'. Bring the engine up to temperature (temperature greater than 80° Χ) from minimum level. Accelerate to 5000 rpm (constant) for about 2-3 seconds and release. Carry out this operation for three consecutive times. With the ignition off, wait 45 s before re-starting the engine (Power Latch function).

Check that the supply voltage to the pump on the pump connector is 13V. Measure the pump absorption current by positioning the ammeter clip for the Examiner on the pump supply cable (on the fuse box or directly on the pump inlet cable [see electrical equipment]); The current measured should be less than or equal to 4.6 Ampere.

- Disconnect the connection from the fuel intake assembly. - Connect using an Examiner in Ohmmeter mode to the connection for the fuel intake assembly at pins 5 and 6 - Read a resistance proportional to the level of the fuel as illustrated in the table below: Fuel level in the tank Resistance value Full tank 33±3 Ohm 3/4 76±3 Ohm 1/2 134±3 Ohm 1/4 206±3 Ohm Reserve 235±3 Ohm Empty 299±3 Ohm Fuel pump assembly pin out Fuel pump assembly

Connect the pressure transducer for the Examiner diagnostic equipment to the return pipe to the tank (1b). Turn the ignition on. Check that, within 10 seconds, that the pressure gauge reading is less than 1 bar. The pump in the tank stops after 10 seconds.

Connect the pressure transducer for the Examiner diagnostic equipment between the diesel filter [1a] and the pressure pump [1b] (connect to the filter outlet). Turn the ignition on. Check, within 10 seconds, that the pressure gauge reading is between 2 and 3 bar. The pump in the tank stops after 10 seconds.

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the fuel injectors. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipe from all the fuel injectors. Restrict the injector recirculation pipe so that no fuel can come out during the test. Turn the ignition key to the start position for 5 seconds and visually inspect that the quantity of recirculation fuel which comes out of the injector connections is more or less the same for all of them, and is very little.

Disconnect the electrical connections from all the fuel injectors. Disconnect the fuel recirculation pipes from all the fuel injectors. Restrict the injector recirculation pipe so that no fuel can come out during the test. Connect the diagnostic equipment (Examiner or Examiner Plus) Connect the diagnostic equipment (Examiner or Examiner Plus) Turn the ignition key to the start (AVV) position for 5 seconds and check that the fuel pressure is over 300 bar with engine speed of about 200 rpm.

Check that the gap between the rpm sensor and the flywheel is between 0.5 and 1.5 mm Check that the rpm sensor resistance is 790 Ohm ± 20% Check that the sensor output signal corresponds to the enclosed graph. 1. Disconnect the pressure sensor from the inlet manifold. Connect tool no. 1.870.752.000 to the inlet manifold. Select the 'pressure gauge' instrument on the Examiner/Examiner Plus and set it to acquire data in 'inlet pressure' mode with full scale of 2000 mmHg and time selection 10 seconds. Go out onto the road (observing the legal speed limits) and carry out the following test. On a stretch of motorway, drive the car at 2000 rpm in 4 th gear. Start graphic acquisition by pressing 'start' on the diagnostic instrument, and after about 2 seconds press the accelerator pedal fully until 3500 rpm is reached. After reaching this speed, release the accelerator pedal fully. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant part, excluding the initial peak, the reading should be 2200 mbar (abpit 1650 mmHg) corresponding to a turbocharging value of 1200 mbar. On a fast non-urban journey, drive the car at 2000 rpm in 3 rd gear. Start graphic acquisition by pressing 'start' on the diagnostic instrument, and after about 2 seconds press the accelerator pedal fully until 3500 rpm is reached. After reaching this speed, release the accelerator pedal fully. Display the resulting graph and in the pressure constant part, excluding the initial peak, the reading should be about 2200 mbar (about 1650 mmHg) corresponding to a turbocharging value of 1200 mbar.

Pin 2, description: track 1 supply, signal type: 5V input. Pin 3, description: track 1 earth, signal type: earth. Pin 4, description: track 1 signal, signal type: analogue output. Pin 5, description: track 2 earth, signal type: earth. Pin 6, description: track 2 signal, signal type: analogue output.

Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment. Display the following in parameter mode: Engine rpm Clutch disc speed Road test the vehicle, at a constant speed (about 30 km/h), without changing gear. Observe the two parameters selected whilst driving Check that there are no significant fluctuations/differences in the clutch speed signal compared with the engine speed.

The amount of oil required for refilling the reservoir completely is 600 cc. The quantity of oil required for refilling the hydraulic system and the reservoir is 700 cc. The check in question is carried out with the oil at ambient temperature (engine cold). Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Make 10 gear changes with the engine switched off (this operation is necessary to collect any traces of oil through recirculation). Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment. Select the 'accumulator depressurisation' service and run. The robotised gearbox reservoir (in the engine compartment) will be full of fluid as a result of the above command. Open the bonnet and check the oil level using the reference marks on the reservoir, after first removing the aluminium cover. If the fluid level is below the MAX mark, note the amount of fluid required to top up.

Visually inspect the pipes, pump, reservoir, hydraulic unit, actuators (engagement/selection, clutch) whilst 50 gear change cycles are carried out from 1st to 5th/R and from 5th/R to 1st (at a rate of 1 gear shift every 3-4 s). Bleed the clutch using the Examiner Plus or Smart (active diagnosis mode).

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment and take a pressure reading. With the pump switched off, the pressure should be between 40.5 and 51 bar at ambient temperature.

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment. Using the Examiner Plus or Smart, check that the battery voltage is above 11.5 V. Make gear changes until the pump is activated. Halt the gear change requests and check how long the electric pump remains activated (listening to the pump and, at the same time, looking at the Examiner Plus or Smart when the 'Pump relay' parameter state changes from ON to OFF). If the battery voltage, at ambient temperature (15-20 ° Χ), is more than 11V and the "Pump relay ON" time is betwee 4 and 14 seconds, the pump is working properly. Repeat the test several times for safety reasons. The operation of the pump could be correct at the time of the test but not during the everyday operation of the vehicle.

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the display of the input state (ON/OFF) for the switch on the brake pedal. Press the brake pedal and check that the value displayed changes.

No accelerator pedal information The signal is received by the Selespeed control unit via the CAN line. Select the CAN information on the Examiner Plus or Smart and check for the presence of any faulty control units. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring for the line, in particular between the faulty control units. Clutch solenoid current Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Selespeed pump Check pump fuse and relay status Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Check pump winding insulation and continuity. Drainage oil accumulator error Replace the accumulator. Lever switch error (any of the four buttons or the Eco/Normal button): Lever check Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the 'LEVER STATUS' display. Make all the selections possible using the buttons on the steering wheel (one at a time) checking that the change in state on the Examiner Plus or Smart is correct; the list of selections to be made is as follows: Lever up (+) (forwards) Lever down (-) (backwards) Lever in neutral (N) Lever in reverse (R) Lever released Check on ECO button Select the input state display (ON/OFF) for the ECO button. Press and release the Economy operation selector button located at the base of the gear lever and at the same time check on the Examiner that there has been a momentary change of state. Select AUTO mode via the lever and at the same time check on the Examiner Plus or Smart that there has been a momentary change of state. Control unit earth error Check the state of the tightening of the earths to the bodyshell and the engine. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Microprocessor 2 error Replace the Robotised Gearbox control unit 2127E10 hydraulic speed selection system control unit - r r Load relay error Check the state of the battery in accordance with the specific procedure. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. In particular check the chain of elements providing the supply for the control unit (wiring, fuses, relays, etc.). Pump relay error Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. In particular, check the chain of elements providing the supply to the pump (fuses, relays, etc.). There are cases where the fastom connectors housed in the relay holder base are detached. CAN network errors Check: that the network monitors all the control units (warning: any control unit connected to the CAN could cause network operating problems). the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring involving the CAN line. It is a good idea not to be restricted to a visual inspection of the connection but to carry out a test subjecting it to mechanical stress (pull the wires, twist them, check the stability of the pins, etc.). Electromagnetic brake (Selection solenoid) Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Odd or even gear engagement (engagement solenoids) Carry out active diagnosis of solenoid valve. If the test is not successful, move on to the next step Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Carry out the active diagnosis of the solenoid valve again. Brake switch The signal is received from the Selespeed control unit either via the wire or via the CAN line. Check the state of the brake switch: Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the display of the input state (ON/OFF) for the switch on the brake pedal. Press the brake pedal and check that the value displayed changes. If there is no change of state, check the switch on the brake pedal, its fastening, its positioning, the state of the connections and the wiring. Clutch sensor Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Engagement sensor (engine off) If this error is present, the gear change and cranking are disabled. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Engagement sensor (engine on) If this error is present, the gear change is slower than usual because the system operates in recovery mode. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Selector sensor If this error is present, the gear change is slower than usual because the system operates in recovery mode. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Clutch plate speed (this signal is detected by the sensor which reads the speed of the main shaft) Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring. Engine speed (from wire) Check connection between engine management control unit and the Robotised Gearbox unit is correct because this signal is sent by the engine management control unit via a dedicated wire. Vehicle speed The signal is received by the Robotised Gearbox control unit via the wire and replicated on the CAN line. Check the state of the connections and the continuity of the wiring.

Check that, with the engine on and the vehicle stationary: it is possible to engage 1 st - 2 nd - R gears using the gear lever with the brake pressed. Check that while moving, all the gears can be engaged depending on the vehicle's speed. With the vehicle stationary, sometimes repeated engagement attempts (retry) are possible due to mechanical sticking of the gears (especially if the gearbox is new). If the phenomenon continues, it is a symptom of a malfunction

1. Connect the Examiner Plus or Smart diagnostic equipment. 2. Start the vehicle and place the gear lever in neutral 3. Use the Examiner Plus or Smart to check whether the clutch disc angular speed is greater than zero (with engine idling) 4. If as under point 3, check clutch is being driven In active diagnosis, carry out the calibration of the clutch parameters through the 'clutch self-calibration enablement'. Repeat points 2 to 4. If the fault does not occur, move on to point 5. 5. If the clutch is not catching, let the engine reach operating temperature and heat up the clutch (with the accelerator pedal pressed beyong halfway). Repeat points 1 to 3 In the conditions described in point 3, check that the clutch is being driven

Turn the ignition key to the ON position. Connect the Examiner diagnostic equipment and select the 'LEVER STATUS' display. Make all the selections possible using the gear lever checking that the change in state on the Examiner is correct; the list of selections to be made is as follows: Lever in neutral (N) (stable position) Lever in reverse (R) (stable position) Lever released (stable position) With the lever in this position (check the state using the Examiner) the following selections can be accessed: Lever in Up position (+) (forwards) (unstable position) Lever in Down position (-) (backwards) (unstable position) Select the Auto/Manual mode (unstable position).

- The diagram below illustrates where the distance between the bracket (B) securing the brake pedal switch (A), located on the pedal assembly and the reaction bracket (C) for the switch push rod, located on the brake pedal should be measured. - Measure the distance between the two brackets and check that it corresponds to the nominal distance of 24 mm.

Discharge the vacuum in the servo unit, with the engine stopped, by pressing and releasing the brake pedal repeatedly and vigorously. With the brake pedal pressed, start the engine without accelerating. Check that after a few seconds, the brake pedal advances in accordance with the increase in pressure brought about by the operation of the servo unit. Release the brake pedal and, without further action, turn off the engine. After about 10 minutes operate the brake pedal, with the engine switched off, and check that when it is pressed for the first time, it lowers with assistance from the servo unit, and that subsequently it gradually becomes harder.

Check that the signal acquired looks the one illustrated without "holes". - Road test the vehicle driving along a straight section at a speed of approximately 50 km/h - Make sure that it will not cause a danger to other traffic and then carry out an emergency stop: the reaction of the system on the brake pedal must be felt.
- Set off from stationary on a slippery surface in order to cause the intervention of the ASR system: the warning light should come on.

- Road test the vehicle looking for an empty square or roundabout. - Making sure that this will not cause a problem or be a danger to other traffic, take a corner in order to activate the ESP system: the ESP warning light has to come on for 2-3 seconds.

- Road test the vehicle driving along a straight section at a speed of approximately 50 km/h. - Make sure that it will not cause a danger to traffic and then steer to the left and the right several times. It is NOT necessary to steer in an exaggerated manner to cause to the ESP warning light to come on.

Road test the vehicle driving along a straight section of road with an even surface at a speed of approximately 50 km/h. Make sure first that it is safe, as regards the traffic situation, and then steer several times to the left and the right trying to reproduce the situation that has produced the error.

- Carry out a road test on traffic free roads in safe conditions following the highway code. - Before proceeding with the test, check the inflation pressure of the two vehicles, restoring the values to the correct ones if they are found to be incorrect. - Carry out the test on an uneven road surface, at a speed of 40 km/h to check the capacity of the suspension to absorb the stresses produced by small imperfections (suspension damping) with the consesquent acoustic repercussions inside the passenger compartment. - Check the capacity of the suspension to absorb the stresses produced on very uneven surfaces with the consequent acoustic repercussions inside the passenger compartment: carry out the test at a speed of 40 km/h on a route that has a succession of man-hole covers. - Check the rapid damping of any pitching produced by the irregularities of the road surface, carrying out the test at a speed of 50 km/h on a straight road with suitably spaced ridges/depressions, This type of test should always be carried out for comparison with a new vehicle or a reference vehicle of the same trim level and engine type, available in the workshop at the time of the test in question. - At the end of the test in question, assess/rate the driving comfort of the vehicle in accordance with the enclosed table. ASSESSMENT RATING Poor 3 Mediocre 4 Just acceptable 5,5 Acceptable 6 Good 7 "The reference vehicle has a driving comfort default rating of 7".

- Carry out a road test on traffic free roads in safe conditions following the highway code. - Before proceeding with the test, check the inflation pressure of the two vehicles, restoring the values to the correct ones if they are found to be incorrect. - Carry out the test on a route where there are left and right hand bends of different degrees, evaluating the laying down speed of the vehicle round the bends, trying to take the bends at a constant speed, avoiding carrying out pull/release manoeuvres. - Evaluate the stability of the vehicle by simulating a lane change/overtaking and check that violent vehicle reactions do not appear leading to unsafe driving during this manoeuvre. - Then carry out a road test on an unmade rod (cobblestones) where there are right/left hand bends of different degrees to evaluate the tendency of the rear of the vehicle to lose grip. - This type of test should always be used for comparison with a new vehicle or reference vehicle of the same trim level and engine type, available in the workshop at the time of the test in question. - At the end of the test in question, assess/rate the behaviour of the vehicle in terms of rolling/pitching in accordance with the enclosed table. ASSESSMENT RATING Poor 3 Mediocre 4 Just acceptable 5,5 Acceptable 6 Good 7 "The reference vehicle has a rolling/pitching default rating of 7".

Connect the recharging device to the air conditioning system in order to read the low pressure (1a) and high pressure (1b) values. Start the engine and run it at idle speed. Deactivate recirculation (led on button off). Press the fan speed increase button until 12 bars are showing on the display. Turn the temperature knobs until they are in the maximum cold position (LOW). Switch off the compressor by pressing the button (both the temperature displays should flash). Check on the recharging device's low and high pressure gauges, that the pressure is within 5 bars for an ET of about 20° C, and about 6 bars for an external temperature ET of about 30° C Activate the air conditioner (led on compressor activation key on). Check that within 1 minute the pressure reaches 2.5 - 3 bar on the low pressure gauge and 15 - 16 bar on the high pressure gauge. Wait for the engine cooling fan to come on. Check that the pressure reaches 1.5 - 1.8 bar on the low pressure gauge and 10 - 12 bar on the high pressure gauge . Check that the engine cooling fan goes off when the high pressure drops to 11-12 bars.

A green coloured cable is associated with the C CAN H network whilst a brown coloured cable is associated with the C CAN L network. A green coloured cable is associated with the C CAN H network whilst a brown coloured cable is associated with the C CAN L network. - If the "communication error present" is found using the Examiner for the fault diagnosis, check whether the NFR node does not see the NBC (NPL), but does see the NGE and the NCR: the problem is probably to be found in the section between the NCR and the NBC. - In support of this theory, it is also necessary to check that the NGE sees the NFR and the NCR but not the NBC and that the NCR sees the NGE but not the NBC.

This test requires the spark gap kit (No. 1806369000). Make sure that the ignition key is in the OFF position. Remove the H.T. coil from its housing. - Check that the map disc is consistent with the vehicle model. - In NAV mode, check that the number of satellites in the last line on the right is at least 3 indicating that the satellite reception is correct. If the reading for the number of satellites is less than 3 then the reception is not good enough to locate the vehicle. It is probably a question of insufficient cover. In this case try and move the vehicle to an area where there is good reception or compare the reception with other cars located in the same place. - The satellite reception test should be carried out in an open area. In this case, without a comparison it is impossible to say whether or not the navigator is defective. If, on the other hand, the comparison reveals even worse reception, check the connection of the satellite aerial, the electrical continuity, the correct power supply and, if necessary, test with different equipment that is definitely working properly. For the road test: Exit in NAV mode Check that the arrow moves consistently with the vehicle speed, otherwise check the presence of the milometer signal. Check that the arrow changes direction in line with the vehicle. If the arrow does not change direction this means that the gyroscope inside the map reader is broken and the Connect should be replaced. Enter a destination and activate the calculation of the route. Wait for the first instruction and the route on the display and check that it is correct. - Irregular instructions: before or after junctions, arrow out of position, they may be due to CD maps that are not up to date: a missing instruction stems from the fact that a road is not on the map because it has not been processed in digital form or the road network has been changed compared with the one on the map. The navigator calculates the position of the vehicle both by means of the satellite signal and using the wheel rpm and the internal gyroscope bush signal. Precision problems may occur when the speedometer and reverse signals are not received correctly. Cases in which the navigator should be disconnected: The vehicle is being transported with the battery disconnected and travelling in a tunnel (the navigator loses the references). Immediately after having changed the tyres (since the wheel rpm/distance conversion factor is not accurate). When replacing the Connect. To initialize the navigator it is necessary to drive about 100 km in optimum satellite reception conditions. If all the tests have not highlighted defects then the problem lies in the Connect which should be replaced.
